# How setTimeout() Works

#### Course: API Handling with Asynchronous Javascript

## How setTimeout() Works

When JavaScript encounters setTimeout(), it:

1. registers the timer,
2. hands the callback function to the browser,
3. and immediately continues executing the next line.

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

In the previous example, console.log("Start"); and console.log("End"); are the synchronous codes.

![Asynchronous Execution in JavaScript](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)

Internally, this is what happens:

1. Start is logged to the console
2. JavaScript encounters setTimeout()
3. JavaScript gives the callback to the Web API
4. JavaScript continues immediately
5. End is logged to the console
6. The browser waits for a minimum of 0 milliseconds
7. The callback becomes eligible to run later
